questions.title: Who will succeed Oleksandr Syrskii as Ukraine's top military commander?
questions.background: Oleksandr Syrskii leads Ukraine's armed forces during the war against Russia.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official announcement by Ukraine's presidency or reliable contemporaneous reporting, including Al Jazeera. Resolution Condition : Resolve when Ukraine's president formally appoints a successor to Oleksandr Syrskii as the country's top military commander. Temporary or acting appointments do not count unless confirmed as permanent. Accepted Answer Format : The successor's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: 2026-07-19 update (Euromaidan Press, Kyiv Post, Ukrainska Pravda, AFP/Straits Times): Amid reports that Zelenskyy is interviewing potential successors to Oleksandr Syrskyi who can ensure a smooth handover along the 1,200 km front, Zelenskyy held a dedicated July 19 meeting with just three senior commanders—Joint Forces Commander Mykhailo Drapatyi, Deputy Chief of the General Staff Volodymyr Horbatiuk, and Air Assault Forces Commander Oleh Apostol—and announced further 'key talks' on July 20. (1) Drapatyi rises (0.45 -> 0.48, kept below 0.50 pending any confirmed ouster) as the only candidate combining Fedorov's endorsement, public pro-reform stance, full operational-strategic front pedigree, and direct inclusion in Zelenskyy's July 19 strategic trio. (2) Andrii Biletskyi rises (0.09 -> 0.11), overtaking Andrii Hnatov for #3: confirmed to have met Zelenskyy on July 17 and explicitly named as Fedorov's second candidate. (3) Chief of General Staff Hnatov drops (0.10 -> 0.07) because Fedorov explicitly sought his removal alongside Syrskyi and Zelenskyy instead met his deputy Horbatiuk on July 19, leaving Hnatov viable mainly if Syrskyi survives this crisis and exits later. (4) Pavlo Palisa holds #2 (0.16) after sitting alongside Zelenskyy during July 18 corps-commander talks (which UP sources said did not directly discuss Syrskyi's dismissal), while Ground Forces chief Hennadii Shapovalov trims slightly (0.07 -> 0.06). Notably, Apostol and Navy chief Oleksiy Neizhpapa publicly defended Syrskyi on July 19, underscoring continued resistance to a shakeup; leaving 12% residual tail for Horbatiuk, Apostol, Prokopenko, Brovdi, Moisiuk, and others.

The protests, led by young people, also exposed deep divisions in the defence leadership on how to stop Russia’s battlefield advances, as the war’s overall momentum has swung in Kyiv’s favour. Syrskyi, 60, faces criticism from civil society, soldiers and lawmakers for his Soviet-style command culture and high casualty tactics. questions.title: If Typhoon Noul makes landfall in mainland China during July 2026, in which province will it do so?
questions.background: Landfall refers to the cyclone's centre crossing the coastline, rather than areas experiencing its wind or rain.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : China's National Meteorological Centre's official landfall report, including reliable news coverage quoting that report. Resolution : Resolve to the province containing the reported location of Typhoon Noul's mainland China landfall during July 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The province's name.
questions.current_reasoning: 2026-07-19 Western Pacific basin update (GMA News/PAGASA July 16-17, Straits Times/CMA July 19): (1) With five days elapsed since July 14 and zero naming of Noul, the residual ~5% chance for the July 14 Guangdong tropical depression is now 0%. (2) PAGASA reported late July 16 that a new tropical depression (45 km/h winds, gusts 55 km/h) formed far outside PAR—2,980 km east of southeastern Mindanao (~153°E)—moving west-northwestward at 20 km/h, a trajectory bringing it near the 135°E PAR boundary around July 20-21 and making it the primary active candidate to intensify into Typhoon Noul. (3) Meanwhile, CMA's July 19 heavy-rain warning depicts a diagonal rain belt from Yunnan to the Yangtze River Delta, locating the Western Pacific Subtropical High (WPSH) ridge axis around ~24-26°N ahead of its typical late-July northward shift. Conditional on Typhoon Noul making mainland China landfall during July 2026, shifting primary weight onto a far-east Philippine Sea (~153°E) WNW-moving genesis—rather than a South China Sea depression—materially boosts Taiwan/East China Sea corridors: Fujian rises (0.25 -> 0.29) to tie Guangdong (0.33 -> 0.29, still heavily weighted for Luzon Strait tracks and any alternate SCS genesis), Zhejiang rises (0.20 -> 0.23), while Hainan (0.10 -> 0.08) and Guangxi (0.05 -> 0.03) trim, leaving 8% residual tail for Shanghai, Jiangsu, Shandong, and Liaoning.

questions.title: Which Indian state will have the highest reported death toll from monsoon floods and landslides as of August 5, 2026?
questions.background: India's annual monsoon can cause fatal floods and landslides across multiple states.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the Indian state with the highest reported cumulative death toll from monsoon floods and landslides since July 1, 2026, according to official data cited in news reporting Resolution Date : August 5, 2026 Accepted Answer Format : The state's name
questions.current_reasoning: 2026-07-19 major empirical & IMD synoptic update (Indian Express, New Indian Express/PTI, Hindustan Times, AFP/Straits Times): (1) IMD confirmed an active monsoon across north, east, and northeast India for the next 6-7 days while forecasting subdued rainfall over west-central and south Peninsular India for the next 7 days (through July 26). (2) Himachal Pradesh rises (0.22 -> 0.26) to #1 after IMD Shimla upgraded warnings to a two-day Red Alert on July 20 (Chamba, Kangra, Mandi, Sirmaur) and July 21 (expanding to Kullu) for extremely heavy rain, flash floods, and landslides, with active rain through July 24 and 70 roads already blocked. (3) Maharashtra drops (0.29 -> 0.24) to #2: its banked early-July toll (~25-35+) remains strong, but subdued western-India rainfall through July 26 leaves its lead exposed to major Himalayan and northern surges. (4) Uttarakhand rises (0.12 -> 0.15) after IMD Dehradun issued a Red Alert for July 20 (Dehradun, Tehri, Haridwar), 2 died from lightning in Haridwar July 19, and landslide-blocked roads jumped to 84. (5) Jammu and Kashmir enters top 5 at 0.09 (replacing Gujarat, which drops into the tail as Surat's ~17 toll stalls under 7-day subdued rain): flash floods and landslides killed at least 18 in J&K on July 19 alone (16 in Poonch, plus Rajouri, with several missing), forcing Amarnath/Vaishno Devi Yatra suspensions amid IMD warnings of extremely heavy rain through July 23; J&K's probability is discounted (~40%) for its constitutional status as a Union Territory rather than one of the 28 states. (6) Uttar Pradesh trims slightly (0.12 -> 0.11) despite a 30-district Orange Alert through July 22, as lightning fatalities may not always count strictly as flood/landslide deaths; leaving 15% tail for Gujarat, Bihar, Assam, West Bengal, Nagaland (8 dead, 4 missing July 19), Kerala, and central India.

local_articles.title: At least 25 killed as floods and landslides hit northern India
local_articles.snippet: At least 25 people have been killed as floods and landslides have hit across north and northeastern India, local officials reported. Several incidents were reported over the weekend in Indian-administered Kashmir and the northeastern state of Nagaland, following days of torrential monsoon rain, officials said on Monday. In Kashmir, rain-related incidents in the Poonch, Rajouri and Doda districts killed at least 15 people, with several others reported missing, a senior police official said. In Nagaland, multiple landslides triggered by persistent rains killed nine people. “We have recovered four of the eight bodies, and rescue work is ongoing,” Wennyei Konyak, the magistrate of Nagaland’s Mon district, told the AFP news agency, adding that at least 15 others had been injured.
